topic: Area C: The World Around Us
subject: french

items.title: When the Academie was founded
items.claim: The Academie francaise was established to regulate the French language. In which year and under whose authority?
items.reveal:
Richelieu gave letters patent on 29 January 1635. The Academie has 40 'immortels' and has been working on its Dictionnaire since 1694 (first edition).

The ninth edition has been in progress since 1986 and was completed in 2024.
items.why: Language regulation in France is a centuries-long state project, not a recent reaction to globalisation.

items.title: What the passe compose replaced
items.claim: In modern spoken French, the passe compose has largely replaced which other tense?
items.reveal_title: Passe simple has retreated to formal writing
items.reveal:
Spoken French uses the passe compose where 19th-century literature used the passe simple. The simple form survives in formal narrative writing, historical writing, and some regional usage.

The shift has been described in detail by linguists since at least Damourette and Pichon (1911-1936).
items.why: Grammatical structures can fall out of speech but persist in writing for generations.

items.title: France and minority languages
items.claim: Which European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages instrument has France signed but not yet ratified?

options.text: France signed in 1999 but has not ratified, citing constitutional issues

items.reveal:
The 1958 Constitution's Article 2 declares 'la langue de la Republique est le francais', cited as an obstacle to ratification.

A 2021 law strengthening regional language teaching was partially overturned by the Constitutional Council.
items.why: Constitutional commitments to a single official language can constrain participation in international minority-language frameworks.
